name: Silver, as plated on a daguerreotype's copper

f0.source: P. B. Johnson and R. W. Christy, 'Optical constants of the noble metals', Phys. Rev. B 6, 4370-4379 (1972), silver n,k as tabulated in refractiveindex.info-database data/main/Ag/nk/Johnson.yml (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/polyanskiy/refractiveindex.info-database/master/database/data/main/Ag/nk/Johnson.yml); cross-check K. M. McPeak et al., 'Plasmonic films can easily be better: Rules and recipes', ACS Photonics 2, 326-333 (2015), data/main/Ag/nk/McPeak.yml; CIE 1931 2-degree CMFs, https://files.cie.co.at/Publications-datasets/CIE_xyz_1931_2deg.csv ; CIE D65, https://files.cie.co.at/Publications-datasets/CIE_std_illum_D65.csv
f0.note: Verified: both n,k tables opened and re-integrated independently; J&C gives [0.98876, 0.98420, 0.97712] (Y 0.9847) and McPeak [0.98937, 0.98780, 0.97840] (Y 0.9875, i.e. 0.987 rather than the stated 0.988), and the spectral checks reproduce. Replaces the Real-Time Rendering Table 9.2 quotation ([0.972, 0.960, 0.915]). Channel envelope of the two measured sets: min [0.989, 0.984, 0.977], max [0.989, 0.988, 0.978]. Both sets are fresh, smooth evaporated films with very low n (about 0.04-0.05), which puts them at the high end for silver. A buffed, aged daguerreotype plate may reflect somewhat less in the blue (surface scatter, incipient sulfide). A measured reflectance of a plate's highlight (Palette research.needed) would settle it.
f0.derivation: Unpolarised normal-incidence Fresnel reflectance R = ((n-1)^2 + k^2)/((n+1)^2 + k^2) from Johnson & Christy's silver n,k (0.3679-0.8211 um), interpolated linearly to 380-780 nm in 10 nm steps, integrated against the CIE 1931 2-degree CMFs under D65, normalised so a perfect reflector has Y = 1, XYZ to linear Rec.709 with the sRGB matrix: [0.9888, 0.9842, 0.9771], Y 0.985. McPeak 2015 template-stripped silver gives [0.9894, 0.9878, 0.9784], Y 0.987. Spectral checks (J&C): R(450) 0.980, R(550) 0.983, R(650) 0.990.

f82.source: P. B. Johnson and R. W. Christy, Phys. Rev. B 6, 4370-4379 (1972), silver n,k via refractiveindex.info-database data/main/Ag/nk/Johnson.yml; cross-check McPeak et al., ACS Photonics 2, 326-333 (2015), data/main/Ag/nk/McPeak.yml; CIE 1931 2-degree CMFs and D65 as for f0
f82.note: Verified by independent recomputation (all three triples reproduce to 4 decimals). Silver's edge is nearly neutral: F82 is slightly below F0 in red and above it in green and blue, so the old 'equal to F0' placeholder was close in form, but its F0 was wrong.
f82.derivation: As f0, but the unpolarised Fresnel reflectance (Rs+Rp)/2 of the complex index at incidence cosine 1/7 (81.79 degrees; Optics.ush MatterConductorFresnel): J&C [0.9870, 0.9862, 0.9863]; at exactly 82 degrees [0.9871, 0.9865, 0.9866]; McPeak [0.9878, 0.9892, 0.9870].
